title: Minimum Operations to Remove Adjacent Ones in Matrix
summary: Given a binary matrix, determine the least number of operations needed to convert it into a well-isolated matrix by flipping any 1 to 0.
statement: Given a binary matrix, determine the least number of operations needed to convert it into a well-isolated matrix by flipping any 1 to 0. A well-isolated matrix has no 1s that are 4-directionally connected to another 1.
constraints: grid is a nonempty binary matrix.
One operation changes one 1 to 0; afterward no horizontal or vertical neighboring pair may both be one.
hints: Occupied cells with adjacency edges form a bipartite graph by checkerboard parity.
By Konig’s theorem, minimum removed vertices equals maximum matching.
Build edges from one parity to occupied neighbors and count successful augmenting paths.
Removing a vertex cover breaks every adjacent-one edge, and bipartite maximum matching has the same minimum size.
editorial: Removing a vertex cover breaks every adjacent-one edge, and bipartite maximum matching has the same minimum size.

tests.explanation: Removing a minimum vertex cover of three occupied cells breaks every adjacent pair.
The ones are already isolated, so zero operations are needed.
